title: Cabinet of sundries - on-call miscellany
content:
Cabinet of sundries — quick, messy on-call crib notes (personal scratchpad)

Purpose
- Throwaway page for tiny procedures, one-off fixes, and shorthand rescue steps when I'm on call.
- Not canonical; migrate anything useful into eng-sre runbooks later.

Top-of-mind checks (5–7 min triage)
1) Grafana: check redwood-core latency and adapter error spikes (last 15m).
2) Pager: read the alert body — what component? region? model id?
3) Recent deploys: `git log --since=\"2 hours ago\" infra/` + check CI status.
4) Active incidents: #incident channel and pinned timeline entry.
5) If CPU/GPU saturation: query autoscaler dashboard (dedicated pool) and increase burst if safe.

Immediate quick fixes (frequently used)
- Restart worker pool (k8s): `kubectl -n inference rollout restart deploy/worker-pool` (only if steady-state errors, not transient).
- Clear prefix cache for X model: `redis-cli -h cache-prod DEL prefix:<model-id>:*` — warn on cache-churn.
- Temporary rollback to previous model tag: update route to model-tag `vN-previous` in routing UI or via API: `curl -X POST .../routes/<route>/target`

Local scripts I use (put under ~/bin during on-call)
- rwi-tail <service> — tails the last 500 lines from service logs (grep for \"ERROR\" and \"WARN\").
- gpu-hog-kill — finds runaway process on node by mem% and `kill -9` (use as absolute last resort).

Escalation cheatmap
- SRE Pager: in-channel ping @sre-oncall (include incident id).
- Serving-runtime lead: Liam Chen (Slack direct).
- Platform infra: Priya Sankar.
- If customer impact and no response within 7m -> page oncall-eng (pager duty).

Common gotchas (past 6 months)
- Model KV cache growth after a burst of long prompts -> latency regressions; workaround: evict largest KV namespaces and restart a subset of pods to force cold starts.
- Autoscaler flapping due to probe misconfig: increase probe timeout from 5s to 15s for adapter v2.
- Tokenization mismatch causing 502s when caller changed delimiter handling — check tokenization tests in model-runner logs.

Temporary config flips (notes for revert)
- 2024-11-09: raised batch-size cap to 512 for route /chat-std -> reduced tail latency but increased variance. Revert plan: set cap back to 256 at quiet window.
- 2024-12-22: enabled fallback-to-small-model on capacity errors (issue JIRA-4412). Monitor quality metrics; revert if >5% quality drop in 24h.

Slack snippets I paste often
- Incident summary: \"Inc <#> — observed X errors -> root cause candidate Y. Action: rolled back Z. Impact: N customers. ETA next update: +15m.\"
- Escalation: \"Paging serving-runtime lead (Liam). Symptoms: sustained 5xxs on /v1/generate, region us-west2, related deploy PR: PR-987.\"

Unresolved TODOs / things to move to proper runbook
- Document exact redis keys used by prefix cache and add safe-eviction script (TBD owner).
- Playbook for partial model cold-start mitigation (step-by-step, who to page).
- Add a health-check endpoint for dedicated GPU nodes that includes KV cache size.

Notes to self
- When using gpu-hog-kill, annotate the node with `ops/last-kill=<timestamp>` to provide context.
- Avoid global cache flush during peak hours; prefer targeted evictions.
- If you revert a model, take heap and GPU profiles before and after.

Scratchpad history (brief)
- 2024-11-12: created — initial checklist and commands.
- 2024-11-23: added autoscaler probe note after incident.
- 2024-12-22: added fallback toggle entry (JIRA-4412).

If nothing else, this file is a brain-dump to keep the midnight handoff coherent. Use it, break it, and move the good bits upstream.

— Maya R.
